The equation is LongTermStress + NoBreaks + TraumaticExperienceTrigger = PTSD.

Unless you were already under long term stress and going without any breaks from it for a few weeks, you won't have PTSD. There's lots of other ways to get fucked up mentally, but it sounds like you are resilient enough to work through it.

Moar PTSD stuff -- other fields hit PTSD, particularly medicine and law, for the same reasons. You get huge workloads, you get sleep deprived and have no breaks, and then some bullshit happens -- usually involving kids -- and it snaps your amgydala/hippocampus connection. The normal mechanism is amgdala sees a threat, starts the flight or fight response, kicks the alarm up to the hippocampus, hippocampus says, "that's not a real threat, that's just a regular plane / picture of a spider / kid laughing" and the amygdala says, "got it, alarm cancelled." When you have PTSD, the amygdala stops listening to the hippocampus and everything is always a life or death situation and you can't get the motherfucker to turn the alarm off even though you know it isn't a real threat.

The most common non-combat PTSD traumatic event is lawyers looking crime scene photos of children, particularly child porn. (Think about that one. Car accident ain't shit against that.)
